threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube app instead of just asking the bus stop sign when the next bus is due. Classic newbie move!
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded us all with a ukulele. The driver just smiled and kept driving, like it was an everyday thing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the smell of grilled kebabs mixed with fresh coffee on a Sunday morning feels like home. You just can't find that anywhere else.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find 24-hour kebab stands that double as makeshift bars after midnight. Where else can you grab a döner and a beer simultaneously?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their tolerance for the BART delays—no one else would casually pull out a book while waiting for 20+ minutes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that stopped for a pigeon to cross, and the driver just smiled. Only in the TL can a bird hold up a city bus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve tapas at any hour, but locals know you won’t find a decent bocata past 11pm. It’s all about the timing.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they stare blankly at the metro map, still trying to decipher the labyrinth of lines and colors.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers by their hesitation at the bus stop, like they're waiting for a tube that doesn't exist here.
Last night on the 3, saw a guy arguing with a lamppost like it owed him money. Brixton can be wild when the sun goes down.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a kid bouncing a soccer ball on the sidewalk while their grandma knitted on the balcony. That blend of old and new feels just right.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, it’s common to see people chilling on the sidewalk at 2 a.m. with their beer, just casually chatting. Feels like a slice of life you won't find elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they avoid the BART at Civic Center without blinking, thanks to the train's random smoke outbursts lately.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Sitting on the 21, a guy serenades us with an off-key version of ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ while the bus screeches to a halt. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think they need to visit Park Güell, but real Gràcians know the hidden gems are the little plazas with local festas during summer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered face while ordering at a local bakery, still trying to figure out the 'pan' vs 'barra' distinction.
